correctness.rationale: Final assessment is for the corrected RESULT.md. The frozen sentence asserting a unique causal stationary state did not specify the sense of stationarity: strict stationarity does not follow from independent centered shocks with fixed variances. For example, alternate a symmetric ±1 shock with a shock taking 2 and −1/2 with probabilities 1/5 and 4/5; these laws have equal variance 1. A strictly stationary state would yield strictly stationary shocks on applying the affine recursion backwards to consecutive state observations, contradicting the different one-time laws. The repaired result states covariance stationarity explicitly, proves existence via the square-integrable causal filter and uniqueness by decay of any bounded-second-moment homogeneous difference, and explains the extra shift-invariance hypothesis for strict stationarity. This preserves the sharp optimization under all original noise-moment hypotheses. The characteristic roots lie on opposite sides of zero inside (−1,1); the adult mean is sb/(1−m), positive exactly on the included allocations. Eliminating the juvenile coordinate gives innovation variance s²v_J+v_A; an independent symbolic solution of the stage-coordinate Lyapunov equations confirms the displayed risk. Below y₀ the logarithmic derivative is negative. Above y₀, T increases as its positive numerator increases and both positive denominator factors decrease; the other derivative term q/[y(y²+q)] decreases strictly. Equivalently Q=y³T/(1−yT) increases up to the endpoint or pole; yT at m is m²/(1−m²), yielding the sharp cutoff and putting equality at the endpoint. At or above m=1/√2, the pole occurs no later than m, so every finite positive q has one interior optimum. Replay: python3 /workspace/replay/checks.py 1 verifies the covariance and derivative identities exactly without using the frozen verifier.
